reason: The text demonstrates the Hebrew people actively and freely expressing their views and concerns. They speak their doubts to Moses (וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה - 'and they said unto Moses'), question his decisions explicitly (מַה־ זֹּאת עָשִׂיתָ לָּנוּ - 'what have you done to us'), cry out their fears (וַיִּצְעֲקוּ - 'and they cried out'), and recount their prior complaints. The only call for silence (תַּחֲרִישׁוּן - 'hold your peace') is a specific instruction to trust God in this moment of deliverance, not a general discouragement from expressing their views. The passage shows no punishment or social pressure against speaking one's mind.
